# pistol golden threat states, v0 — the oracle for the threat generator's whole
# query surface (docs/decisions.md D-243, D-256, D-259).
#
# Pinned by SHA-256 in crates/pistol-solver/tests/threat_query_tests.rs
# (THREAT_V0_SHA256). Editing this file without updating that constant in the
# same commit is a red test, which is the point: a golden file that can drift
# quietly is not golden. Pass threshold, pre-registered: every case, every
# answer, every run. There is no partial credit on a query.
#
# WHAT KIND OF FILE THIS IS: MACHINE-DERIVED, hand-maintained in nothing but the
# `plies` lines. Every expectation is what the from-scratch reference in
# `tests/common/reference.rs` prints for that ply list, and the test
# `threat_v0_is_what_the_reference_prints` renders all of them and compares them
# with these bytes. So the file is reproducible from the repository — no scratch
# generator stands behind it — and an edited expectation is a red test rather
# than a re-hash. That makes this a THIRD KIND beside its neighbours:
# `bench_positions_v1.txt` is produced by a shipped binary, and `tactical_v0.txt`
# is hand-authored and its content IS the specification.
#
# The reference shares only pistol-core and is cross-checked on every case
# against an independent bounding-box region scan. It was also compared value for
# value against a reference written by a different session for the design this
# file implements: 336 of 336 AGREED, counting the values present on both sides.
# THAT COMPARISON DID NOT REACH EVERY ROW HERE, and this says so where the claim
# is made: the other record carries no `raise_cells`, lists win-in-one-ply CELLS
# where this file lists windows, and names no window on a `canwin ... oneply`
# record. Those three row kinds rest on the region scan and on the regeneration
# above. Nothing here was read off the code it tests.
#
# THE POSITIONS ARE LEGAL PLY SEQUENCES. Each `plies` line is played through
# `GameState::from_plies`, so legality, turn structure and phase come from
# pistol-core and not from a fixture author's belief. Turn 1 is one stone at the
# origin (rule 3), so every list starts at 0,0 — for the distant-cluster case
# that stone is padding with a bridge out to q = 42. Padding stones sit at hex
# distance >= WIN_LEN from every cluster cell and from each other, which is
# exactly the condition under which no window can hold a padding stone and a
# cluster stone at once.
#
# Format. One record per case; `#` to end of line is a comment. Every `expect`
# key below is required exactly once — a record missing one is refused by name,
# because a fixture whose expectations are silently incomplete is a fixture that
# passes by omission (docs/decisions.md D-37).
#
#   case    <name>                        starts a record; the name is its identity
#   plies   <q,r> ...                     the stones, in play order
#   expect  <side> hot          <axis>@<q,r> ... | -    live, own >= 4
#   expect  <side> win1         ...                     live, own == 5
#   expect  <side> completed    ...                     own == WIN_LEN
#   expect  <side> live3        ...                     live, own == 3
#   expect  <side> live2        ...                     live, own == 2
#   expect  <side> threat_cells <q,r> ... | -           empties of the hot windows
#   expect  <side> raise_cells  <q,r> ... | -           empties of the live3 windows
#   expect  <side> cover  <1|2> nothing | impossible | {<q,r>} {<q,r> <q,r>} ...
#   expect  <side> canwin <1|2> none | oneply <q,r> <axis>@<q,r>
#                                       | pair <q,r> <q,r> <axis>@<q,r>
#   expect  state  to_move <side> phase <First|Second> stones_owed <n>
#                  outcome ongoing | outcome win <side> turn <n>
#   end                                   closes the record
#
# A `cover` or `canwin` row is read from the side that OWNS the threat: `p1
# cover 2` is `blocking_covers(P2, Two)` — what P2 would have to play to answer
# P1's hot windows. Keeping every row of a record about one side's threats is
# what makes a record readable; the defender is always the other one.
#
# `cover` has THREE spellings because `Cover` has three variants and they are
# not interchangeable: `nothing` is NothingToBlock, meaning there is no hot
# window to answer; `impossible` is Impossible, meaning no cover within the
# budget exists; a brace list is Minimal and is never empty. A fixture that
# could not tell the first two apart could not pin the distinction the type
# exists for.
#
# `canwin` carries the WITNESS WINDOW as well as the cells, because the witness
# selection rule names it: a cell can be the single empty of more than one
# five-window, so an implementation that picked a different window would still
# agree on the cell.
#
# Axis names follow docs/decisions.md D-33 — an axis is named for the coordinate
# that stays constant along it: ConstQ has direction (0,+1), ConstR (+1,0),
# ConstS (+1,-1), where s = -q - r.

case single_hot_window
plies 0,0 -1,0 -5,6 1,0 2,0 1,6 3,-6 3,0
expect p1 hot          ConstR@0,0
expect p1 win1         -
expect p1 completed    -
expect p1 live3        ConstR@1,0
expect p1 live2        ConstR@2,0
expect p1 threat_cells 4,0 5,0
expect p1 raise_cells  4,0 5,0 6,0
expect p1 cover 1      {4,0} {5,0}
expect p1 cover 2      {4,0} {5,0}
expect p1 canwin 1     none
expect p1 canwin 2     pair 4,0 5,0 ConstR@0,0
expect p2 hot          -
expect p2 win1         -
expect p2 completed    -
expect p2 live3        -
expect p2 live2        -
expect p2 threat_cells -
expect p2 raise_cells  -
expect p2 cover 1      nothing
expect p2 cover 2      nothing
expect p2 canwin 1     none
expect p2 canwin 2     none
expect state  to_move p1 phase Second stones_owed 1 outcome ongoing
end

case overlapping_hot_windows_one_shared_cell
plies 0,0 -1,0 -5,6 1,0 2,0 1,6 4,-6 4,0 6,0 7,6 10,-6 7,0
expect p1 hot          ConstR@0,0 ConstR@1,0 ConstR@2,0
expect p1 win1         -
expect p1 completed    -
expect p1 live3        ConstR@3,0 ConstR@4,0
expect p1 live2        ConstR@5,0 ConstR@6,0
expect p1 threat_cells 3,0 5,0
expect p1 raise_cells  3,0 5,0 8,0 9,0
expect p1 cover 1      {3,0} {5,0}
expect p1 cover 2      {3,0} {5,0}
expect p1 canwin 1     none
expect p1 canwin 2     pair 3,0 5,0 ConstR@0,0
expect p2 hot          -
expect p2 win1         -
expect p2 completed    -
expect p2 live3        -
expect p2 live2        -
expect p2 threat_cells -
expect p2 raise_cells  -
expect p2 cover 1      nothing
expect p2 cover 2      nothing
expect p2 canwin 1     none
expect p2 canwin 2     none
expect state  to_move p1 phase Second stones_owed 1 outcome ongoing
end

case true_double_threat
plies 0,0 -5,6 1,-6 1,0 2,0 1,6 7,-6 3,0 0,14 -1,20 -6,26 0,20 1,20 0,26 6,14 2,20 3,20
expect p1 hot          ConstR@-2,0 ConstR@-1,0 ConstR@0,0 ConstR@0,20
expect p1 win1         -
expect p1 completed    -
expect p1 live3        ConstR@-3,0 ConstR@1,0 ConstR@1,20
expect p1 live2        ConstR@-4,0 ConstR@2,0 ConstR@2,20
expect p1 threat_cells -2,0 -1,0 4,0 4,20 5,0 5,20
expect p1 raise_cells  -3,0 -2,0 -1,0 4,0 4,20 5,0 5,20 6,0 6,20
expect p1 cover 1      impossible
expect p1 cover 2      impossible
expect p1 canwin 1     none
expect p1 canwin 2     pair -2,0 -1,0 ConstR@-2,0
expect p2 hot          -
expect p2 win1         -
expect p2 completed    -
expect p2 live3        -
expect p2 live2        -
expect p2 threat_cells -
expect p2 raise_cells  -
expect p2 cover 1      nothing
expect p2 cover 2      nothing
expect p2 canwin 1     none
expect p2 canwin 2     none
expect state  to_move p2 phase First stones_owed 2 outcome ongoing
end

case win_in_one_ply_each_side
plies 0,0 0,8 1,8 1,0 2,0 2,8 3,8 3,0 4,0 4,8

expect p1 completed    -
expect p1 live3        ConstR@-3,0 ConstR@2,0
expect p1 live2        ConstR@-4,0 ConstR@3,0
expect p1 threat_cells -2,0 -1,0 5,0 6,0
expect p1 raise_cells  -3,0 -2,0 -1,0 5,0 6,0 7,0
expect p1 cover 1      impossible
expect p1 cover 2      {-1,0 5,0}
expect p1 canwin 1     oneply -1,0 ConstR@-1,0
expect p1 canwin 2     oneply -1,0 ConstR@-1,0
expect p2 hot          ConstR@-2,8 ConstR@-1,8 ConstR@0,8 ConstR@1,8
expect p2 win1         ConstR@-1,8 ConstR@0,8
expect p2 completed    -
expect p2 live3        ConstR@-3,8 ConstR@2,8
expect p2 live2        ConstR@-4,8 ConstR@3,8
expect p2 threat_cells -2,8 -1,8 5,8 6,8
expect p2 raise_cells  -3,8 -2,8 -1,8 5,8 6,8 7,8
expect p2 cover 1      impossible
expect p2 cover 2      {-1,8 5,8}
expect p2 canwin 1     oneply -1,8 ConstR@-1,8
expect p2 canwin 2     oneply -1,8 ConstR@-1,8
expect state  to_move p2 phase Second stones_owed 1 outcome ongoing
end

end
